text:
Aisha Rahman: Quick topic 1 adaptive "confidence-aware" quant scheduler for production. Idea: budget our low-bit paths by expected quality loss instead of fixed percent rollout.
Diego Ramos: Curious. So allocate FP8/INT4 capacity to request slices predicted to be robust?
Aisha Rahman: Exactly. Use a cheap estimator at request time (e.g., prefix logit SNR + prompt length + token-entropy) to score risk. High-risk -> route to safer variant. Low-risk -> go to aggressive quant.
Kenji Ito: Estimator cost must be tiny. We can't add another model call. Could compute prefix SNR from first N tokens using cached KV stats.
Nora Patel: Also think about cold-start where no KV cache. Fallback heuristic: short prompts < 32 tokens -> aggressive cheap path, long prompts -> safer.
Diego Ramos: How do we measure "expected quality loss"? KL vs fp32? or task-specific metric?
Aisha Rahman: Start with proxy: logit-space KL (quant vs fp32) on a probe set, map to observed downstream metric (e.g., exact-match or BLEU on test prompts). Build a small regression to predict metric drop from KL + SNR.
Kenji Ito: That mapping will be model-dependent. Need per-model calibrations.
Aisha Rahman: Yep. We'll version calibrations by model+quant-profile. Tag them like `qa:v1|fp8-legacy`.
Nora Patel: Telemetry names proposal: `quant.scheduler.score`, `quant.scheduler.route`, `quant.scheduler.expected_loss`, `quant.scheduler.model_variant`. Keep them numeric where possible.
Diego Ramos: Ops: what about privacy? We shouldn't sample full outputs for enterprise tenants unless permitted.
Aisha Rahman: Agreed. Default aggregated counters only. Per-tenant raw diffs opt-in for enterprise.
ops-bot: Resource check: sampling job quota available on offline-cluster 03:00-07:00 UTC. Estimated artifacts 120GB for 50k probes.
Nora Patel: Great. Config example (proposal):
```yaml
# quant-scheduler config (prototype)
scoring:
  method: prefix_snr
  prefix_len: 16
  model_weights: {snr: 0.6, length: 0.2, entropy: 0.2}
routes:
  - name: aggressive_fp8
    max_qps: 500
    score_threshold: 0.7
  - name: safe_int8
    max_qps: 2000
    score_threshold: 0.4
  - name: fp32_fallback
    max_qps: 10000
    score_threshold: 0.0
metrics:
  report_aggregate: true
  per_customer_slices: false
```
Diego Ramos: Who owns the scheduler code? Is this runtime or router team?
Kenji Ito: Runtime needs the hooks (fast scoring API + route hints). Router team implements policy. We should have a small shim in runtime that exposes `score_hint` and `route_hint`.
Aisha Rahman: Minimal API: `score_hint(inputs) -> float` and `route_hint(score) -> variant_name`. Keep deterministic and cheap.
Nora Patel: Canary plan: offline calibration -> staging shadow 1% traffic for 48h -> canary 5% with auto-fallback to safe variant on any alert.
Diego Ramos: Alerts: P95 latency increase > 10% OR downstream error spike (task-specific) OR expected_loss > configured budget.
Kenji Ito: Implementation detail: avoid cascading overloads. If aggressive_fp8 hits max_qps, fall back to safe_int8, not fp32, unless safe_int8 saturated.
QA-bot: Suggestion: include unit tests that simulate adversarial prompts where SNR is misleading (e.g., low-entropy but wrong fact).
Aisha Rahman: Good call. We'll add adversarial probe set to calibration suite.
Diego Ramos: Timeline and owners?
Aisha Rahman: Proto in 2 weeks (scoring shim + offline calibrations) - owner: me. Router policy + canary plan in 3 weeks - owner: Kenji. Dashboards + alerts - owner: Nora.
Nora Patel: I'll add Grafana panels: score distribution, route split, expected_loss by model.
Kenji Ito: One more: randomize routing for identical scores within epsilon to avoid hot-paths. Use small jitter seed per request.
Aisha Rahman: Decision summary: proceed with confidence-aware scheduler spike. Deliverables: scoring shim, offline calibration dataset + mapping, staging 1% shadow, canary playbook.
Diego Ramos: :thumbsup:
Nora Patel: I'll file the runbook and link the dashboard once ready.
Aisha Rahman: Thanks all 1 will open PRs and a short RFC doc.
